findings.text: SEMANTICS FAITHFUL + NO BLOCKING HOLE (the crux judgment). The refinement narrows the tier floor from 'any footprint spanning >= 2 declared areas -> high' to 'any touched pair with no allow-listed edge in either direction -> high', staying standard only for a CLIQUE of modeled pairs. This is a faithful implementation of the founder decision (2026-07-22): cohesive breadth over modeled edges no longer forces approval (the rubber stamp is removed), while every genuinely unmodeled coupling still elevates. Over the real contract, 19 of 28 pairs and every superset containing an unmodeled pair still elevate; only 12 multi-area sets (all cliques of modeled couplings) pass as standard. I could not construct a case where a genuinely unmodeled cross-area coupling is laundered to standard: the rule is monotonic non-decreasing in the touched set, so a no-edge pair cannot be hidden by adding areas, and no non-clique multi-area set stays standard.

EITHER-DIRECTION coarsening (the one residual permissiveness, assessed non-blocking). _areas_connected treats {A,B} as cohesive if EITHER A->B or B->A is allow-listed. So a change touching {contracts, fleet} whose ACTUAL new coupling were the REVERSE direction (contracts depending on fleet - a layering inversion the contract does not model, since only fleet->contracts is allowed) would NOT elevate. This is a real coarsening, but it is NOT a hole that defeats the founder's safety intent, for three independent reasons: (1) footprint_tier_floor operates on declared AREA MEMBERSHIP from footprint globs, not on import direction - it structurally cannot see which way a coupling points, so no elaboration-time rule short of over-approximating all breadth (the rejected old rule) could catch a reverse-direction coupling; (2) directional import enforcement is the explicitly-deferred job of WARP-1102 (W2, gate-time footprint-versus-diff), and the contract's dependencies block is currently enforcement: review, so directional violations are not gate-mechanized for ANYONE yet, regardless of tier; (3) the either-direction reading is the AC's and the founder decision's verbatim wording ('no allow-listed edge between them in either direction'). Recommendation for a human eye: when WARP-1102 lands the directional import check, confirm it (not the tier floor) is the surface that refuses a reverse-direction coupling; the tier floor deliberately does not.

DIRECT-vs-TRANSITIVE (open, honestly disclosed, errs strict). The rule tests only the DIRECT allow-listed edge, not transitive reachability, so a pair reachable only through a hub (e.g. fleet and metrics, both ->contracts) is treated as a boundary crossing and ELEVATES. This is the SAFE direction (more elevation, not less) and cannot open a hole; it may over-elevate some transitively-cohesive changes, which is a conservative-not-dangerous posture the founder decision does not forbid. Whether transitive cohesion should count is explicitly left open in the spec Out-of-scope and the proof assumptions - honest.

DEFERRALS honest (NG5). New-module detection stays deferred to WARP-1102 (W2) and is named in the footprint_tier_floor docstring, the spec_placement_footprint capability note, spec Out-of-scope, and AC5; a footprint glob matching no declared area contributes no area and cannot elevate on its own, which is the case W2's diff machinery is needed for. Footprint UNDER-declaration (declaring a single area to keep a genuinely cross-area change off the floor) is a pre-existing declaration-trust limitation of the whole placement mechanism, also W2's footprint-versus-diff job; WARP-1011 neither introduces nor worsens it. The capability note is accurate to what ships. One cosmetic observation (non-blocking): the shipped WARP-1103 spec's front-matter risk JUSTIFICATION prose still describes the old coarse rule ('a boundary-crossing change is at least high'); the recorded risk high remains correct-as-shipped and the artifact is deliberately frozen (forward-only), but a human eye may wish to note the prose predates the refinement. The builder flagged this in proof assumptions[2].
